# Udumbarika Sutta (DN 25 (PTS DN iii 36))

**ID:** DN 25 (PTS DN iii 36)  
**Section:** Dīghanikāya (dn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Udumbarika Sutta  
**PTS:** DN iii 36  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0103m.mul1.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0103m.mul1.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In modern scholarship, the sutta was analyzed extensively by Mark Allon as a case study of mnemonic repetition and prose formulas in the Pali Canon [Allon 1997].

Curated parallels include Chinese translations preserved in the *Dīrghāgama* (DĀ 8), the *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 104), and the individual translation T 11 (*Nijutuo fanzhi jing*) [1953]. Within the Pali Canon, parallels and shared thematic pericopes on asceticism are found in the *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (DN 8 and MN 12), the *Cūḷadhammasamādāna Sutta* (MN 45), the *Kandaraka Sutta* (MN 51), the *Apaṇṇaka Sutta* (MN 60), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3.156–162, AN 4.198), with references also occurring in the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 15) and *Puggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4).

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: DA 8 散陀那; MA 104 優曇婆邏; T 11 尼拘陀梵志
- Passage-level parallels: DN 8 (PTS DN i 161) Mahāsīhanāda Sutta; MN 12 (PTS MN i 68) Mahāsīhanāda Sutta; MN 45 (PTS MN i 305) Cūḷadhammasamādāna Sutta; MN 51 (PTS MN i 339) Kandaraka Sutta; MN 60 (PTS MN i 400) Apaṇṇaka Sutta; an3.156-162 Acelakavagga; AN 4.198 Attantapasutta
- Mentioned in: Mnd 15 Attadaṇḍasuttaniddesa; Pp 2.4 Catukkapuggalapaññatti

**Sources**

- [1953] 1953 [English translation of Chinese Dīrghāgama/Madhyama Āgama parallel] — Parallel narrative of Sandhāna visiting Queen Udumbarikā's grove and the dialogue with Nyagrodha.
- [Anālayo 2019] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Mindfulness of Breathing: A Practice Guide and Translations (2019) — Discussion of wanderers scoffing at the Buddha's preference for silence and seclusion.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Overview of sutta position in DN and discussion of ascetic practices and the true recluse.
- [Piyadassi 1979] Piyadassi Thera, ed., Felicitation Volume to Narada Mahathera (1979) — Quotation of the Buddha's declaration to Nigrodha regarding his purpose in teaching.
- [Allon 1997] Mark Allon, Style and Function (1997) — Stylistic analysis, opening passage, and calculation of word count and mnemonic abbreviations.
- [Walshe 1987] Maurice Walshe, The Long Discourses of the Buddha: A Translation of the Dīgha Nikāya (1987) — Summary of Nigrodha's challenge, defeat, reaching the pith beyond asceticism, and setting at Queen Udumbarikā's park.
